body.p: The owner (2026-10-28): the standard (ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025, bought by the owner) cannot be committed, so sxml writes a comprehensive conformance suite of its own from it. No public Schematron conformance suite of that scope is known; check (SchXslt's own tests, schematron.com, the Schematron community's repositories) and record what exists and its licence before writing; reuse with attribution what a licence allows.

item.p: Whom it serves: 7.28 (its gate), every later change to Schematron in sxml, and other implementations if the owner publishes it. Who pays: test files and a coverage list; no code in the library.

The standard's text is data, not repository content: cite clause numbers, paraphrase in a few words; never copy sentences, examples or schemas from it. The extracted text is in the orchestrator's scratchpad (iso-19757-3/standard.txt), never committed.
Layout (tests/schematron/, imitating the QT4 catalog of third_party/qt4tests: a catalog, test sets, test cases):

catalog.xml naming the test sets; one test set per clause group (schema structure, patterns and rules, assertions and reports, let and parameters, abstract patterns and extends, inclusion, phases and from, diagnostics and properties, name and value-of, group, library and rules, visit-each, severity/role/flag and their dynamic evaluation, query bindings, documents, schematronEdition, SVRL, static errors);

each test case: the clause it covers, a schema (inline or a file), one or more instance documents, an optional phase and parameters, and the expected result, written neutrally (no sxml API, no sxml error codes): the set of findings (kind assert or report, id, the location as a node path, role, flag, severity, the message text after value-of and name), or "the schema is in error" (with the clause that makes it so), or "implementation-defined" with the clause that allows it;

coverage.xml: every normative requirement of the standard (each "shall" and each definition that constrains behaviour), as clause number plus a short paraphrase, with the test cases covering it; a requirement without a test is listed as such.

Cross-checks: every case using only 3rd-edition constructs runs through SchXslt 1.10.1 on sxml (compile with the release CLI, which now has no step limit; ) and must agree, or the disagreement is recorded with the clause that decides it. 2025-only cases are checked by a second, independent agent that derives each expected result from the clause without seeing the first one's answer.

Owns: tests/schematron/ (new), a README there (format, licence, how to run the cross-check), a glossary term if needed, a D-record. Not the driver: 7.28 writes the driver that runs the suite against sxml.

Done when: coverage.xml lists every normative requirement of clauses 4 to 7 and the annexes that are normative, each with at least one test (or a recorded reason); all cases are well-formed and validate against a schema for the catalog format; the SchXslt cross-check agrees on every 3rd-edition case or each difference is recorded; the independent check of the 2025-only cases is recorded; 7.28's gates name the suite (pass rate 100 % of applicable cases). Done 2026-10-28 (): 514 cases in 18 sets (tests/schematron/), 139 requirements in coverage.xml (131 with cases, 8 with reasons), an edge-case table of construct by dimension, the ambiguities of the standard in the README; SchXslt cross-check of the 369 2020 cases (281 agree, the rest decided by recorded clauses); all 145 2025-only cases checked independently in two rounds, none changed.
